narrative.overview: Friends gather around one rectangular wooden table, whether passing one phone or joining a room. The table itself is the Feast table chosen on 2026-11-25 (`.impeccable/mocks/table-avatars/index.html?v=a`, built as `src/ui/table/TableScene.jsx`), which replaces the earlier Joinery mock's flat plank panel: a lamplit tabletop with a thick rim; players sit along its long sides as emblem avatars; ordinary controls remain easy to read beside or below it. On a shared phone, keep the private card covered until its deliberate handoff. Preserve the mock’s English, Thai, and German layouts and its light and dark modes. The tavern comes from the table, the warm wood palettes, and the party gathered around it. Keep the rest of the page and controls calm, legible surfaces. Do not spread plank stripes across the page or ordinary control panels. Use the exact approved table arrangement and interaction states as the source for the hub rebuild and carry its table language into every Imposter screen.
keyCharacteristics: Five wood palettes, each with light and dark mode; Oak is the default.
Each wood carries its own warm-metal accent for actions; green and red identify the two sides.
Rectangular plank table, long-side seating, covered private card, readable controls.
System sans typography with Thai-capable faces; 52px minimum primary tap targets.

rules.name: The Accent Follows The Wood Rule
rules.body: The wood's accent marks something to tap or a current interactive state; it is never blue and never borrowed from another wood. Green and red communicate sides, never generic emphasis.

rules.name: The Table Holds The Texture Rule
rules.body: Visible plank construction belongs to the tabletop. Do not texture the page background or ordinary panels.

rules.name: The Name Stays Readable Rule
rules.body: Player names, room codes, and action labels stay horizontal, wrap safely, and never become texture or ornament.

dos: Do use the feast table scene (owner's choice, 2026-11-25) for the table, long-side seats and emblem avatars, with the covered private card and actions beside or below it.
Do keep the table as the one strongly textured surface; use wood tones without page-wide stripes.
Do keep controls, player names, status text, and the wood itself distinct at every mode and language.
Do respect 52px touch targets, visible keyboard focus, and `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: Don't use the superseded Neighborhood Noticeboard hierarchy or its separate hub/game styles.
Don't add decoration, texture, or motion that lowers contrast or implies a state that is not true.
